title: Sebastian and the Orchard
premise: In the river city of Vellamare, Isandro Nakamura has spent twelve years as a typeface cutter's daughter, mastering the silences that keep her family safe inside the Aldering print shop. When the winter bridge closes and revolution severs the city in two, she discovers her late mother's hidden letters revealing a promise made to General Corvane's son — now the enemy officer holding the far bank: an orchard deed that could save both families or destroy them. As the print shop is conscripted to forge propaganda and her father's loyalty is tested against the truth of what he helped bury, Isandro must choose between the silence that protected her and the truth that might free everyone. She crosses the frozen river at last light, delivers the deed, and loses the orchard itself to fire — but gains a family stitched from both banks, carrying the story forward in printed word rather than blood.
about_author: Tamsin Sterling is the pen name of a former letterpress apprentice who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in coastal mill towns. Their novels explore how ordinary tradespeople survive the collisions of history.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sorts
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the Aldering print shop, she cuts type beside her father and catalogs the small silences that keep their household safe. The emotional beat is quiet dread: rumors of the bridge closing arrive with the autumn ink shipment.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, flashback woven through present. She recalls the night her mother died and the promise extracted from her father — never speak of the Nakamura orchard across the river. Beat: grief hardened into habit.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge on the bridge square as soldiers chain the gates for the season. Isandro watches a Corvane officer on the far bank and feels inexplicably seen. Beat: the world contracts; escape routes vanish.

chapters.title: Letters Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Hunting for packing paper, she finds her mother's hidden correspondence — proof of a peacetime promise to the Corvane heir regarding the orchard deed. Beat: vertigo; everything she knew about her mother tilts.

chapters.title: What Father Cut Away
chapters.summary: Father's POV. He recognizes the missing letters and confesses partially: he helped hide the deed years ago to protect the family from Corvane debts. Beat: love tangled with cowardice.

chapters.title: The Conscription Order
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Revolutionary authorities commandeer the print shop to produce propaganda; her father must comply or be marked. Beat: the trade that sheltered them becomes an instrument of the conflict.

chapters.title: A Name in the Galley
chapters.summary: Apprentice Tomas's POV. Setting type for a denunciation list, he spots the name of the shop's old friend Mireille. He brings it to Isandro instead of the foreman. Beat: first crack in collective silence.

chapters.title: The Officer at the Window
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. During a parley at the bridge gate, she speaks briefly with Lieutenant Elias Corvane, who mentions 'the orchard' — testing whether the promise survived his father's fall from grace. Beat: recognition and terror entwined.

chapters.title: Mireille in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Isandro and Tomas's POV alternating. They hide Mireille beneath the paper store; she reveals the revolutionaries know about the Corvane deed and want it as leverage. Beat: loyalty begins pulling in three directions.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Father's POV. Pressured to print a false account of a massacre, he complies — then burns one page of the true record, keeping it like a relic. Beat: complicity deepens; self-forgiveness fails.

chapters.title: The Deed's True Wording
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Deciphering her mother's hand, she realizes the deed names heirs of both families jointly — meaning the war itself cannot legally dispossess either side. Beat: hope arrives disguised as paperwork.

chapters.title: Winter Takes the River
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating brief POVs. Ice locks the river; food thins; Mireille's fever rises; Tomas is questioned by the committee. Beat: pressure without release, the city holding its breath.

chapters.title: The Committee Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A revolutionary auditor searches the shop and nearly finds the letters; her father lies fluently for the first time in his life. Beat: the protector becomes the risk.

chapters.title: What Mireille Saw
chapters.summary: Mireille's POV, fevered and lucid by turns. She recounts witnessing the original signing of the promise — and that the committee's leader was there too, and betrayed it. Beat: truth revealed as weaponizable.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The auditor offers a bargain: the deed in exchange for the family's safety and Mireille's release to prison. Beat: the cost of every choice made explicit; Isandro asks for three days.

chapters.title: Learning the Ice
chapters.summary: Tomas and Isandro's POV. They secretly test the frozen river's crossing points at night, guided by a ferryman's old chart hidden in a type case. Beat: fear transmuted into purpose; found family consolidates.

chapters.title: The Night of the Long Proof
chapters.summary: Print shop ensemble POV. To buy time, they set and print a forged 'original' of the deed while keeping the true one hidden — each character cut feeling like perjury. Beat: craft turned to deception; guilt shared openly at last.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Case
chapters.summary: Foreman Hessler's POV. Cornered by the committee, Hessler reveals the crossing plan. Mireille is taken; the forged deed is seized. Beat: betrayal born not of malice but exhaustion — the theme's darkest note.

chapters.title: Crossing at Last Light
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. With hours before the exchange, she crosses the ice alone with the true deed to reach Elias Corvane before the committee can stage its trap. Beat: terror, resolve, and the promise finally kept mid-stride.

chapters.title: The Orchard Burns
chapters.summary: Alternating Isandro and Elias POV. The committee raids the orchard the same night; the house burns, but the joint-heir deed, read aloud before witnesses on both banks, forces a stand-down. Beat: climax — victory purchased with loss.

chapters.title: Setting the Record
chapters.summary: Isandro and Father's POV. Back in the shop, they print the true history — the promise, the betrayal, the fire — under both families' names, and the committee, exposed, collapses. Beat: truth replacing silence as protection.

chapters.title: Spring Thaw
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, epilogue tone. The bridge reopens; the scorched orchard is planted anew by hands from both banks, Tomas apprenticed beside her, Mireille home. Beat: found family rooted where blood once divided; memory kept in type.
